thread:
sam: Hey team — hitting a weird onboarding snag. Starter app shows WebSocket 'connected' in browser, but the first API call returns 402 Payment Required. Workspace in the console says 'Pending billing'. Repro: clone starter, npm i, export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key-from-welcome-email>, npm start. Browser console prints 'handshake ok' then the fetch returns 402. Anyone seen WS succeed but REST blocked on billing?

alana: @sam yep I've seen variants. Usually billing gating blocks token use until a payment method is added. Strange that WS handshake still succeeds though — that suggests the handshake path bypasses the same gate. Can you paste the exact error body from the network tab?

sam: Error body (copied):
```json
{
  "error": "billing_required",
  "message": "Workspace billing not configured: first call blocked"
}
```
Also screenshot: app shows chat input enabled for a second then an error toast.

jess: This sounds like the short-circuit we noticed in the workshop last week. There was a bug where the client-side websocket code shows 'connected' after the socket handshake but the REST token check runs later and fails. People assume the app is ready because of that quick WS message.

marco: Another angle — are you using the personal welcome key or a workspace service key? If the welcome key is scoped to an org that hasn't accepted the billing invite, REST endpoints can be blocked while the websocket handshake (which is a lighter auth check) succeeds. Check the token scope in the dev console.

sam: I'm using the key from the welcome email (looks like a workspace key). In the CLI `redwood whoami` it prints: "org: example-org (pending)". So sounds like invite/billing state.

deploy-bot: :information_source: deploy 29876: added temporary console flag to show 'Billing required' banner for pending orgs.

alana: Workarounds: 1) Add a payment method to the org in the console; 2) create a new workspace and accept its invite (quicker for workshop attendees); 3) dev teams can flip the internal dev flag to allow first-call for test workspaces. I'll open a DX ticket to make the quickstart explicitly check org billing before showing the app UI.

jess: Filed DEVX-612: "quickstart should check org billing / invite acceptance before enabling UI" and added repro steps + screenshot. Also proposed small client fix: on client boot, call `GET /v1/org` and if state !== 'active' show an overlay explaining the billing/invite steps.

sam: Thanks — that overlay would save a bunch of confusion during onboarding sessions. I'll link the PR once I push the patch to starter.

jess: Nice — added note to the quickstart README to check the 'Pending billing' banner and the invite acceptance in the console.

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter/pull/45 (adds org-state check + clearer error UX) :rocket:

marco: Follow-up for infra: we should unify the auth gating so websocket and REST enforce the same state to avoid the false-positive 'connected' message. I'll add a follow-up ticket for runtime.

alana: Agreed. Also adding a tiny telemetry event to capture how often 'WS connected but first call fails' happens so we can measure impact.

sam: Great, thanks everyone — will test once PR merges. :thumbsup:
